newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds bounce up on U.S. treasury fall.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds bounce up on U.S. treasury fall.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed up sharply in hearty volume Friday as the U.S. 30-year treasury bond dipped below 6 3/4 after weaker than expected American jobs data, traders said.
"The rise was in large part due to the rise in the U.S. rate on the back of the explosive jobs figure," a trader said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 skipped up $0.60 to 119.30, and Argentina's FRB due 2005 gained 5/8 to 85 1/8.
Argentine bonds have also been shored up by a bout of government determination to push through a fiscal austerity package and more flexible labor laws.

"The government has recently become tougher on issues it had been dragging its feet on, and this makes the fiscal side look a lot more attractive," the trader said, "And there's the backing from the International Monetary Fund as well."
He added that there was no reason that Argentine bonds should not start Monday in bullish mood as well.
"We still regard the market as positive, as long as nothing unusual happens over the weekend," he said.

The U.S Labor Department reported September non-farm payrolls fell by 40,000 against an expected rise of 166,000. But analysts noted that average hourly earnings rose by 0.5 percent against a forecast 0.2 percent, and that the average working week was also slightly longer than expected.
Argentine interbank call money was flat from Thursday at 6.875 percent.
